We  have seasons because of the  tilt of Earth's axis. As  Earth orbits around the sun , this tilt causes different  parts of the planet to receive more or less direct  sunlight at different times of the year.

When  your part of Earth is  tilted toward the sun, the  sun's rays hit more  directly and spread over a smaller area,  so you get more heat an d longer days. That's summer . Six months later, when your part of  the planet is tilted away from the sun , the rays come in at  a lower angle and sprea d over a larger area, giving  you less heat and shorter days. That's winter .

Spring and fall happen  in between, when the tilt is neither  toward nor away from the sun, so  you get moderate temperatures and day lengths in  between the extremes. 

Interestingly, it's not actually  Earth's distance from the sun that causes  seasons, even though we 're a bit closer in  January than in July. The t ilt is what really matters,  which is why it's winter  in the Southern Hemisphere when  it's summer in the North.
